claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
HCL code can be converted to Pulumi.
Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together.
A `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource, taking `bucket` and `key` arguments, exists in the Pulumi Terraform provider for referencing Terraform state stored in S3.
`pulumi.StackReference` takes a stack name and exposes `getOutput` to read outputs from another stack.
`S3Reference` objects expose a `getOutput` method for reading outputs of the referenced Terraform state.
`aws.ecs.Cluster` accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties, and `logging: "DEFAULT"` is a valid value.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
The `pulumi import` CLI syntax takes a resource type token (e.g. `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc`), a resource name, and a resource ID as positional arguments.
Pulumi supports transferring state ownership gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, with `validateResourceOfType(aws.ec2.Instance, (instance, args, reportViolation) => ...)` as the callback signature.
`enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` is a valid policy enforcement level in Pulumi policy packs.
Pulumi policies can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".
Pulumi's Automation API is imported in TypeScript via `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.
`pulumi.LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` accepts `stackName`, `projectName`, and `program` in the Automation API.
`pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible from the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import in TypeScript.
In the Automation API, `stack.setConfig(key, {value})` sets stack config and `stack.up({ onOutput })` deploys the stack and returns a result with `outputs`.
The Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
Component resources can be used to create reusable components that integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving multi-tool complexity to platform teams.
The `@pulumi/terraform` package exists and provides `terraform.state.S3Reference`.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` constructor is called via `super(type, name, {}, opts)` with type `custom:WebApplication`.

The `aws.lb.LoadBalancer`, `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition`, and `aws.ecs.Service` resources accept the properties used in the example (loadBalancerType, internal, networkMode, requiresCompatibilities, cpu, memory, containerDefinitions, launchType, networkConfiguration.assignPublicIp).
A page exists at /docs/intro/concepts/ titled 'Pulumi Architecture & Concepts' that dives into Pulumi's architecture.
A page exists at /docs/using-pulumi/adopting-pulumi/ providing comprehensive migration strategies.
A page exists at /docs/intro/vs/terraform/ providing a detailed comparison of Pulumi and Terraform features.
A page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/ about the Automation API.
A page exists at /docs/insights/policy/ about Policy as Code.

A Mercedes-Benz case study exists at pulumi.com/case-studies/mercedes-benz/ describing large-scale infrastructure modernization and platform engineering.
A Lemonade case study exists at pulumi.com/case-studies/lemonade/ describing rapid development with Pulumi and Terraform.
